title: User Management and Authentication
summary: Covers local/domain user flows, role assignment, auth modes, and account lifecycle operations.
coverage: Create, edit, disable, and reset user access
Domain user onboarding and sync considerations

warning.title: IMPORTANT
paragraphs: Role and permission changes are enforced on subsequent authorization checks. A user can lose route visibility immediately after access is reduced.

sections.title: Identity model and credential storage
paragraphs: RAPTOR keeps the existing login page. The backend validates username and password against Keycloak using a confidential direct-grant client (`raptor-login`). Passwords are not stored in Postgres.

Keycloak is the identity source of truth: realm role `raptor-access` is the allowlist, composite realm roles map to RAPTOR `user` / `pentester` / `manager` / `admin`, and optional permissions are client roles on `raptor-login`. Postgres `allowed_users` is a write-through cache used for collaborators, audit, and request-path authorization.

Directory users can exist in Keycloak via LDAP/AD user federation or another Keycloak identity provider, but they cannot sign in until an admin adds them in Settings (which assigns `raptor-access`). The Keycloak admin console is not the supported operator UI. RAPTOR login remains a username/password form (Keycloak direct grant), so password-capable federations such as LDAP/AD work after allowlisting. Broker-only OIDC/SAML users can be allowlisted once they exist in Keycloak; they cannot use the RAPTOR password form unless that identity also has a password Keycloak can validate.

sections.title: LDAP onboarding flow
paragraphs: Directory onboarding is handled from `User Management -> Add LDAP Users`. Admins search Keycloak (LDAP user federation plus any other user-storage providers and already-imported identity-provider users). Results can be supplemented from a direct LDAP search when `LDAP_SERVER` is set. Staging selected identities, assigning role and optional permissions, and submitting in batch assigns `raptor-access` so a password-capable federated user can sign in.

Add does not create a second local Keycloak password user. Exact username lookup imports the LDAP account into Keycloak when federation is connected. If the identity is not in Keycloak yet, add fails until federation or the identity provider has imported them.

Set `LDAP_SERVER`, `LDAP_DOMAIN`, `LDAP_USER`, and `LDAP_PASS` on the app environment so bootstrap can register the `raptor-ldap` user-storage provider. Optional knobs: `LDAP_USERS_DN`, `LDAP_VENDOR`, `LDAP_USE_SSL`, `LDAP_START_TLS`, `LDAP_TRUSTSTORE` (default `never` for private CAs). Optional OIDC/SAML broker: `KEYCLOAK_IDP_ALIAS` plus `KEYCLOAK_IDP_PROVIDER` and the matching issuer or SAML URLs. Additional providers can be added in Keycloak; RAPTOR search and allowlisting still apply.
The backend normalizes usernames to lowercase and validates role and permission payloads before insert. Duplicate identity insert attempts fail at the database uniqueness layer.
orderedList: Run `Search` with a non-empty query, which calls `GET /ldap-search?query=...`.
Select one or more directory users from search results.
Assign a role per selected user and set optional permissions allowed for that role.
Submit the batch, which calls `POST /add-user` for each selected entry.
Verify new entries in `Existing Users` with correct `auth_type` and effective role.

sections.title: Local user onboarding flow
paragraphs: Local user creation is used when LDAP is not available or when a controlled local account is required. The flow lives in `User Management -> Add Local Users`.
On create, RAPTOR creates a Keycloak user with a temporary password and `UPDATE_PASSWORD`, stores a cache row in `allowed_users`, and returns the temporary password once in the response payload.

sections.title: Role and optional permission governance
paragraphs: RAPTOR applies role defaults and then merges role-allowed optional permissions. Optional permissions outside the allowed set are stripped by backend sanitization. `create_manual_records`, `view_pentest_page`, and `delete_records` cannot be granted as optional extensions.
For `user`, `view_security_dashboard` opens the pentest board (`/pentest`) only. It does not grant host notebooks, scan-live, or `/apps/:id`.
When role is updated through `POST /update-user-role`, backend resets stored optional permissions to an empty list. Admins should reapply optional permissions explicitly after role transition.

sections.title: Existing user maintenance actions
paragraphs: Existing user cards expose role and optional permission editing in a single dialog. Save triggers role update first when changed, then permission save with role-aware normalization.
Deletion permanently removes the user row from `allowed_users`. Use deletion only when access should be fully removed, not for temporary suspension.

sections.title: Authentication reset and session edge cases
paragraphs: Password reset is policy-enforced for bootstrap admin and newly created local users. Login uses Keycloak brute-force protection and RAPTOR session-expiry protections that can block access even with correct credentials.
Common failure paths should be handled before deeper troubleshooting to reduce time spent on permission or route assumptions.
